summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY. Built bare-metal C firmware on STM32 Cortex-M4 with interrupt-driven GPIO, ADC, and I2C drivers, and RTOS based control software using FreeRTOS with mutex-synchronized tasks across sensor and motor control pipelines. Comfortable working across the full hardware software stack, from UART and I2C sensor integration to hardware-software validation on physical test rigs.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with a Raspberry Pi over Bluetooth; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and hardware-software integration end-to-end.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to an STM32 microcontroller over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART command handling and manual user override.
Ran FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X time of flight sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed STM32 Cortex-M4 peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1), achieving 3.68 KB Flash and 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.
Built timer-synchronized ADC scan conversions and interrupt-driven sample capture for real-time temperature sensing.
Implemented a low-level I2C driver and real-time display update loop entirely in embedded C, with no RTOS or HAL dependencies.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) across a distributed Jetson and Arduino controller pipeline; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++, driving five servos with range-gated contact detection.
Integrated dual VL53L0X time of flight sensors via a TCA9548A I2C multiplexer for contact-aware grasping, combining a camera range gate with a gripper-triggered stop at 25 mm.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
